doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Navy bands at Great Lakes and the Pacific
summary: He describes the A, B and C bands, being shipped to Hawaii with the Hellcats, and air raid alerts.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So the Navy band was stationed where?
Great Lakes. There was three bands, A band, B band, and C band.
I thought you went to Hawaii or someplace.
Oh, that’s where they shipped me out.
So you never got – at that time, there was no fighting there or anything like that?

Oh yeah. We went on. They were still bombing. The war was pretty thick in ’42. With the men, they just put us on the E deck – that’s A B C D E – and then turned the lock. I said, boy. And then they have these alerts when you were in the E deck.
You mean the air raid things and all that?
